title: Security review - Encryption & KMS (BYOK/HSM)
next_steps: Send KMS architecture diagram and BYOK onboarding guide (Redwood)
Share SOC 2 Type II report and audit-logs sample schema (Redwood)
Schedule a demo of HSM-backed key rotation with NovaPay infra (week of 2026-06-24)

action_items: Jenna Cole: Share BYOK & HSM integration doc + example terraform (due: 2026-06-20)

transcript:
[00:00] Jenna Cole: Hey everyone, thanks for joining \u2014 I see Leah, Rajat, Tom, and Marcus from our side. Quick sound check.
[00:05] Leah Ortiz: Yep, good here.
[00:07] Rajat Mehra: All good.
[00:10] Marcus Li: Great. So agenda is encryption at rest + in transit, KMS/BYOK options, HSM support, and then audit logs / compliance mapping. We'll leave time for Qs.
[00:20] Jenna Cole: I'll kick off with a very short overview of how Redwood treats keys and encryption, then Marcus will do the deeper technical parts.
[00:30] Rajat Mehra: Sounds good \u2014 high level first \u2014 major constraint for us is that customer data must be encrypted with our keys, we need proof of key custody, and the keys should be rotated under our control.
[00:40] Leah Ortiz: And we have to show audit trails for key usage for SOC 2 and upcoming ISO attestation.
[00:45] Marcus Li: Totally. At a high level Redwood supports three models: Redwood-managed keys (default), Customer-managed keys in cloud KMS (CMEK/BYOK), and HSM-backed BYOK (we call that BYOK+HSM or EKM). Each has tradeoffs.
[00:58] Tom Nguyen: Can you clarify what you mean by "Redwood-managed"? Is that multi-tenant?
[01:02] Marcus Li: Yes, Redwood-managed means we hold the master key material in our KMS cluster which is multi-tenant but encrypted at rest and isolated per-customer in our key hierarchy. We do envelope encryption: per-tenant data keys are encrypted with a master root key.
[01:14] Rajat Mehra: Envelope encryption model \u2014 ok. But for NovaPay we want CMEK where our KMS is the root and Redwood never has the raw root key.
[01:22] Jenna Cole: Absolutely \u2014 CMEK/BYOK is a supported path. In that case you provision a key in your cloud KMS, grant Redwood a usage principal for encrypt/decrypt, and we do envelope encryption using your key to wrap data keys.
[01:33] Leah Ortiz: Does Redwood support key import into HSM (i.e., we generate keys on-prem or in our HSM and upload)?
[01:38] Marcus Li: We support both importable keys and HSM-backed keys depending on the provider. There are two common patterns: 1) Customer imports an existing key into AWS KMS/Google KMS \u2014 some providers support import (note: imported keys might not be HSM-protected in the same way), 2) Use a cloud HSM or external EKM where the key material never leaves the HSM. For strict FIPS/HSM requirements, we recommend EKM/HSM where Redwood calls the KMS to perform wrap/unwrap and the key material stays in the HSM.
[01:59] Tom Nguyen: Is there a latency impact when every RPM call needs to contact the HSM? We have high QPS on embeddings routes.
[02:06] Marcus Li: Good question. We mitigate latency with envelope encryption: only data key wrap/unwrap happens against the customer key in KMS/HSM \u2014 that occurs at key generation and during rotation, not per token. Runtime token encryption/decryption uses data keys cached in the runtime. So HSM calls are infrequent.
[02:25] Rajat Mehra: What about signing operations or model artifacts? We also want model weights checksummed and signed so we can prove integrity.
[02:31] Marcus Li: We can integrate artifact signing via customer KMS too; we sign manifests with a key that you control. We also emit an audit log entry for each signing operation.
[02:38] Leah Ortiz: Speaking of audit logs \u2014 what do those look like? Are they tamper-evident?
[02:43] Jenna Cole: We stream audit logs to a customer-configured S3 bucket or Cloud Storage via a secured delivery pipeline. Logs include timestamp, operation (wrap/unwrap, decrypt, sign), principal, request id, and request metadata. They are signed and can be retained per customer policy. We can also integrate with your SIEM.
[02:58] Tom Nguyen: Are logs available in near real-time? We need them for incident response.
[03:01] Marcus Li: Yes, near real-time delivery \u2014 usually within seconds to a couple minutes depending on destination. We support SSE and VPC endpoints for log delivery.
[03:09] Leah Ortiz: For SOC 2 evidence we'd need chain of custody and key rotation history. Does Redwood keep rotation metadata?
[03:15] Marcus Li: Yes, rotation events, key versioning, and access grants are all recorded in the audit logs. We can provide a rotation history export for audits.
[03:23] Rajat Mehra: How does RBAC and SSO tie into this? We want least privilege so only a small set of Redwood service principals can call our KMS.
[03:30] Jenna Cole: For RBAC we integrate with your IAM through defined service principals or cross-account roles. We encourage creating a dedicated role for Redwood with limited KMS permissions (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey only) and no key deletion rights. For console or support access we enforce RBAC within Redwood and SSO via SAML/Okta or OIDC.
[03:47] Leah Ortiz: Are there policies or example IAM permission JSONs you can share?
[03:51] Jenna Cole: Yes we'll attach sample IAM policies in the follow-up. (Link: https://redwood.example.com/sec/kms-byo k \u2014 note: deck shared)
[04:01] Tom Nguyen: What's the model when customers want an on-prem HSM that is not in AWS/GCP? Can you call an on-prem HSM over our network?
[04:08] Marcus Li: We support EKM over secure channels \u2014 Redwood can call an external key manager via a TLS-mutual authenticated endpoint in your VPC. That requires setting up connectivity and allowing Redwood's egress IPs or using PrivateLink. There is additional network setup and latency considerations but it's supported for Private deployments.
[04:26] Rajat Mehra: So for our timeline, we want HSM-backed keys and full audit logs. We also want an SLA for cryptographic operations and documented key rotation. Is that all doable in Dedicated or Private only, or also Hosted?
[04:38] Jenna Cole: Hosted can do BYOK with most cloud KMS providers. For external on-prem HSM EKM patterns, that's usually Private or Dedicated with a private control plane (we need network routing). For the strictest isolation policies and PII residency, Private is recommended.
[04:52] Leah Ortiz: Any regulatory issues with key escrow or Redwood holding key material? We can't allow escrow.
[04:56] Marcus Li: With BYOK + HSM the customer keeps control \u2014 Redwood never has raw root key material. We can support key deletion and strong audit controls. We have contractual options for key custody terms.
[05:07] Tom Nguyen: Does Redwood support KMS providers other than AWS? We're on Azure and have Azure Key Vault with HSM.
[05:12] Marcus Li: Yes, we support AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault, and external HSM/EKM providers. Implementation details differ slightly but the envelope model and audit/control policies are consistent.
[05:22] Rajat Mehra: For key rotation, can we enforce our rotation schedule and rotate keys without downtime?
[05:27] Marcus Li: Yes \u2014 we support zero-downtime rotation: we generate a new data key and gradually rewrap/decrypt as needed; since we keep multiple key versions for a grace period, reads can still decrypt old ciphertext until rewrap completes. We coordinate rotations with the customer for compliance windows.
[05:42] Leah Ortiz: Is there any open-source agent we need to run in our VPC for the EKM?
[05:46] Jenna Cole: For most EKM use cases we don't require a customer agent. We connect to your KMS via a private endpoint. For very air-gapped customers we offer a deployable connector that can run in your environment. We'll share that doc.
[05:58] Tom Nguyen: Can we control retention of decrypted payloads in logs and disable certain fields?
[06:03] Marcus Li: Yes \u2014 we have redaction rules and field-level controls for audit logs and request/response capture. You can opt out of storing full request payloads, keep only metadata, or redact PII fields before logs are emitted.
[06:16] Jenna Cole: Quick note on encryption in transit: TLS 1.2+ enforced, mTLS available for Private deployments, and we support TLS termination within a dedicated VPC.
[06:25] Rajat Mehra: Great. Any concerns about tokenization or KV cache being exposed? We saw a note about KV cache in your docs.
[06:31] Marcus Li: KV cache is an in-memory structure in the serving runtime; it's encrypted at rest and not persisted unless configured. We can disable caching for specific customers or routes.
[06:41] Leah Ortiz: One more question on compliance: do you have SOC 2 and ISO reports?
[06:45] Jenna Cole: Yes \u2014 Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is pursuing ISO 27001. We'll share the latest reports in the next email.
[06:52] Tom Nguyen: Ok if we run a pilot, what's the quickest path \u2014 BYOK with Azure Key Vault?
[06:57] Marcus Li: That would be fastest \u2014 provision a key in Azure Key Vault, create a service principal with encrypt/decrypt/generateDataKey, provide the ARN/ID to us, we configure the envelope wrapping. We can stand up a pilot in Dedicated or Hosted depending on your data residency needs.
[07:12] Jenna Cole: Recap / next steps: we'll share BYOK/HSM integration docs, sample IAM policies, SOC 2 report, and schedule a demo week of 6/24. Marcus will prepare a short latency note. Leah will send required audit fields.
[07:24] Rajat Mehra: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:26] Leah Ortiz: Thanks \u2014 appreciate the clarity.
[07:28] Jenna Cole: Thanks all, we'll follow up by email with the links.
[07:30] (call ends)
